acceptance_criteria.criterion: The "Resume Run" button appears when: no run is currently active, project status is not COMPLETE or ARCHIVED, run metadata exists with a valid thread_id, dry_run === false, and result !== "SUCCESS".
The button does not appear when a run is currently active (pending or started in the queue).
The button does not appear when project status is COMPLETE or ARCHIVED.
The button does not appear when dry_run === true in the metadata.
The button does not appear when result === "SUCCESS" in the metadata.
Clicking the button calls API.orchestratorStart(planPath, false, threadId) and the request body contains resumeThreadId set to the metadata file's thread_id.
The button disappears once the queue poll returns a new active run entry.

summary: Reviewed all three modified files: api-client.js, project-detail.js, styles.css.
All 7 acceptance criteria verified at the implementation level — guard chain logic is correct and all conditions are evaluated in the right order.
AC-2 (no button when run is active): confirmed — resume button code lives entirely inside the `else` of `if (activeFilename)`, so it cannot fire while a run is active.
AC-4/AC-5: dry_run and result guards evaluated after the API call, in the correct promise callback chain.

AC-6: orchestratorStart(planPath, false, threadId) confirmed; resumeThreadId is conditionally included via `if (resumeThreadId !== undefined) body.resumeThreadId = resumeThreadId` — backward-compatible.
AC-7: pollResume uses Router._clearPolling() + renderProjectDetail() on first active queue entry — correct teardown and re-render.

CSS: .btn base class sets `border: 1px solid transparent`; .btn-resume correctly overrides only border-color, giving the outlined primary-color style. .btn-resume:hover { opacity: 1 } correctly overrides the .btn:hover { opacity: 0.85 } fade via cascade order. Dark theme compatibility achieved through CSS variable usage.
No blocking issues found. Two low-priority observations recorded. One documentation-forward tag for the Documentation agent.

comments.note: project-detail.js (resume button click handler): The error-banner creation block (getElementById + createElement + append) is duplicated verbatim in both the `else` branch (result.started falsy) and the `.catch` handler. Extracting this into a local `showResumeError(msg)` helper would halve the boilerplate and make error path changes a one-touch edit. Non-blocking — behavior is identical in both branches.

project-detail.js: The pollResume closure checks `effectiveStatus === 'pending' || effectiveStatus === 'started'` to detect a new active entry. This is correct for current queue semantics but is independent of the `activeFilename` check used in the main `pollQueue` path. If a third effectiveStatus ever denotes 'active', both polling closures would need updating. Consider extracting a shared `isActiveQueueEntry(entry)` predicate when either closure is next touched.

[documentation-forward] api-client.js: API.getRunMetadata(slug) and the three-argument form of API.orchestratorStart(planPath, dryRun, resumeThreadId) are not yet covered by api-client.test.ts. The Documentation agent should ensure these two additions are reflected in the API surface documentation and that test coverage recommendations are recorded.
